hook_text: Two hundred years ago, surgeons were praised for how fast they could cut off a leg. Why did speed matter so much?
clip_script: An operating theatre long ago: no painkillers, patients held down, dirty coats, and many dying of infection afterwards. Then come the breakthroughs. 1846: ether puts patients to sleep. 1865: Joseph Lister uses carbolic acid to kill germs. 1895: Wilhelm Röntgen discovers X-rays. 1901: Karl Landsteiner discovers blood groups, making safe transfusions possible. Today's operating theatre: asleep, sterile, safe.
visual_style: Whiteboard split scene: a grim old operating room on the left, a clean modern theatre on the right, with four icons in between: a mask, a spray bottle, a blood bag and an X-ray of a hand.
mood: Dramatic at first, then relieved and impressed.
pacing: A grim opening, then one breakthrough at a time with its date and hero.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make a timeline of the four discoveries that made surgery possible.
